content.title: About
content.content: Sorghum, puffed is a light, crunchy puff made from whole sorghum grains through high‑pressure heat treatment. Sorghum (Sorghum bicolor) is a drought‑tolerant cereal native to Africa and now cultivated in many warm regions worldwide. The puffs have a neutral, slightly sweet flavor and a crisp texture, making them a convenient snack or ingredient.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sorghum is one of the most drought‑resistant crops, thriving with minimal irrigation.
Unlike corn, sorghum is naturally gluten‑free, suitable for gluten‑free diets.
Traditional African and Asian cuisines have used sorghum for centuries before modern puffed snacks existed.
Puffed sorghum is often used in children's foods because of its easy digestibility.
Sorghum grains are rich in antioxidants, especially phenolic compounds that give the grain its dark hue.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Sorghum provides both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion and satiety.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: The grain contains iron, which contributes to normal hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Puffed sorghum has a lower glycemic index than many corn‑based snacks, helping to moderate blood sugar spikes.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium in sorghum supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phenolic compounds act as antioxidants, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Cereal allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to sorghum, especially if they react to other grains.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; moderate consumption is advised.

items.title: Added ingredients
items.content: Commercial varieties may contain added sugar or salt, which should be considered in a controlled diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Puffed sorghum can be enjoyed as a snack, mixed into granola, yogurt, smoothies, baked into bars, or used as a crunchy topping for salads and soups.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the puffs in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent fat oxidation.
